results.reason: Issue 1 says the Varga stock purchase is a Change of Control requiring Crestline's prior written consent under §15.4. It says the Disclosure Schedule (Part 3.5, item 3.4) wrongly labels the Crestline agreement 'Notice only; no consent required'. It also explains the resulting termination right and fee, and that the SPA §3.5 consents representation would be inaccurate.

Issue 7 notes that Crestline may assign to an Affiliate or Qualified Transferee under §14.2 without Halvorsen's consent, and that this 'could also introduce a competitor of Varga'. It never analyzes the §1.1 Qualified Transferee definition (any distributor of lab or diagnostic products in the Territory). It also does not explain that the definition fails to exclude Halvorsen competitors or their affiliates.

Issue 6 explains that the Amendment restates §12.3 so only §9 breaches are excluded. It says this drops the §10 and §11 carve-outs, so those claims, including Halvorsen's claims against Crestline, are now capped. However, it does not cite the §17.5 order-of-precedence clause as the reason the amendment controls. Applied strictly, this omission should fail the criterion; see the corrected result in the final output.
The response states that the original §12.3 excluded from the caps breaches of Sections 9 and 10 and the indemnification obligations under Section 11.
The response states that §12.2 caps aggregate liability at amounts paid or payable to Supplier in the preceding 12 months.
The response is a memo with separately numbered issues. Each issue has 'Where it appears' (document and section), 'Why it matters', and 'Recommended fix'.
The response concludes that consent is required, not merely notice.
The response concludes that the §10 and §11 carve-outs were removed by the Amendment.
